pictūra , ae, f. pingo,
I.painting, the art of painting.
I. Lit.: “una est ars ratioque picturae,” Cic. de Or. 3, 7, 26 ; 1, 16, 73; id. Brut. 18, 70; App. Mund. p. 66, 23.—
B. In partic., a painting of the face, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 105.—
C. Transf., concr., a painting, picture (cf. tabula): “et si qua inutilis pictura sit, eam vendat,” Plaut. As. 4, 1, 10 ; Cic. Or. 11, 36: nego ullam picturam neque in tabulis neque textilem fuisse, quin conquisierit, id. Verr. 2, 4, 1, § 1: “accedant statuae et picturae,” Sen. Ep. 16, 8 : “positae sunt picturae Herculis liberos occidentis,” id. Contr. 5, 34, 14 : “statuas et picturas avehere,” Tac. A. 16, 23 : “dicitur tabulam picturae cedere,” Gai. Inst. 2, 78 .—Of embroideries: “textilibus picturis,” Lucr. 2, 35 .—Of paintings in Mosaic, Verg. Cul. 64.—Of a carving in relief: “et sculpsit in eis picturam cherubim,” Vulg. 3 Reg. 6, 32 .—
II. Trop., a painting, picture in words: “animum ab istā picturā imaginibusque virtutum traducere,” Cic. Tusc. 5, 5, 14 : Homerum tradunt caecum fuisse; “at ejus picturam, non poësin videmus,” id. ib. 5, 39, 114 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
